title: Svelte components with exported props
summary: Build a product card that receives its data through export let and scopes its own styles.

scenario.briefing: The storefront repeats product markup on three pages. Build one card component that receives a name and a price, renders both, and keeps its styles with the component.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Declare price with export let and the number type.
Put the name and price inside the article element.
Format the price with price.toFixed(2) inside braces.
Keep the existing style block and add a rule for the price.

misconceptions.description: Reassigning an exported prop to update the parent.
misconceptions.feedback: The parent owns the value. Send an event or accept a callback when the child needs to request a change.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Reassigning an exported prop updates the child's local value and warns; it does not change the parent.

misconceptions.description: Relying on a global selector to style the card.
misconceptions.feedback: Svelte scopes the style block to the component. Keep the card rules there so other pages cannot override or inherit them.

misconceptions.description: Believing reassigning an exported prop changes the parent variable.
misconceptions.feedback: The parent owns the value. A child assignment changes only its local view and does not update the parent.

sections.title: export let declares a prop
sections.body: In a Svelte component, an exported let declaration becomes a prop. The parent passes name and price as attributes, and the component reads them like local variables.

sections.title: Markup is the render function
sections.body: Svelte compiles the template into DOM updates. Curly braces insert values, and the compiler updates only the text that depends on a changed prop.

sections.title: Styles stay with the component
sections.body: A style block is scoped to the component by default. The compiler adds a class to the markup and rewrites the selectors, so .product-card cannot leak into another page.

vocabulary.definition: A value a parent passes to a component through an exported declaration.
A curly-brace expression in markup that renders a value.
A style rule the compiler limits to the component's own elements.

steps.title: Render props in a Svelte component
steps.prompt: Edit ProductCard.svelte. Export the name and price props, render both in the markup, and keep the card styles in the component style block.

files.content: {name}

tests.description: The markup renders the name and a two-decimal price.

hints: Declare export let name: string and export let price: number.
Render {name} in the heading and {price.toFixed(2)} in a paragraph.
Keep the article class and the scoped style block.
Remove the TODO and leave the component styles local.

steps.explanation: Props enter through export let and stay owned by the parent. Markup renders them with braces, and the compiler keeps style rules local to the component.
hints: Check whether each statement treats exported props as parent-owned.
Confirm that Svelte scopes style blocks by default.
Reject the claim that a child assignment updates the parent.
Select statements about props, scoped styles, and compiled markup.
